learning_outcomes.text: Students will be provided with the mathematical foundations necessary for the study of computer science.
Students will learn mathematical culture, way of thinking, and argumentation in mathematics, as well as basic proof techniques.
Students will have built a broad base of examples, on which they can demonstrate concepts and methods in mathematics, and also in other subjects, e.g. programming.
Students will have practical skills in working with concepts in discrete mathematics.

syllabus_topics: Basic enumeration principles and combinatorial configurations.
Basic combinatorial identities: Pascal's formula, binomial and multinomial theorems.
direct and indirect proofs, proof by contradiction,
(Illustrated on basic number theory: divisibility, prime numbers, etc.)
Binary relations: basic concepts, composition of relations, reverse relations.
Mappings: basic concepts, composition of functions, discrete functions used in computer science.

assessment_methods.method: Continuous assessment (graded homework, quizzes, activities in exercises, tests)

assessment_rules: The student must obtain at least 55% of points from the semester continuous assessment to take the final exam. The student must obtain at least 50% from the written part of the final exam. Approximate scale for grading: A 90%, B 80%, C 70%, D 60%, E 55%.
